title: Deployment briefing: daily tether & annotated issues log (draft)
content:
Overview:
This doc is the daily briefing and operational tether for the upcoming deployment window (07/16 -> 07/17 UTC). Purpose: give operators a concise preflight checklist, a minute-by-minute cadence for the first 8 hours of rollout, a short rollback decision matrix, and an annotated issues log we can expand into the post-release retro. Status: draft — want rapid review from infra, serving-runtime, and SRE before 07/15 EOD.

Goals and constraints:
- Launch target: routing change + model config roll (v3.1 -> v3.2) for hosted_api-prod.
- SLO constraints: p50 latency +5% allowed, p95 max +15% for first 2 hours; error rate must remain <0.5%.
- Canary budget: start 1% traffic, expand to 5% (30m), 20% (90m), 50% (3h), 100% (6h) if no triggers.
- Golden metrics: token-per-request cost delta, generation median latency, 95th percentile mem pressure, request error rate, KV cache hit ratio.

Pre-merge checklist (ops owner notes) — quick pass before merging release branch:
- [ ] PR LGTM + CI green (Arjun)
- [ ] Perf regression check: compare perf-run-2027-07-02 vs main (bench script) (Kenji)
- [ ] Canary model artifact pinned in catalog with hash and quant profile (Sofia)
- [ ] Configs baked: autoscale thresholds, batch-size caps, prefix-cache TTLs (infra ops)
- [ ] Run smoke suite on staging with 1k synthetic sessions (smoke-v3.2) (SRE)
- [ ] Alert tests: simulate 5% error injection to ensure on-call gets page (ops lead)
- [ ] Release notes draft pushed to marketing repo (see section below)

Launch-day cadence (first 8 hours) — compact timeline:
- T-30m: Final go/no-go call on #shipday-ops. Confirm on-call roster and runbook links.
- T-10m: Freeze merges to prod branch; scale-instrumentation marker toggle on.
- T+0: Merge and trigger deploy pipeline (orchestration). Start canary at 1% traffic.
- T+5m: Verify health endpoints across canary nodes (startup latency, KV load).
- T+15m: Check telemetry dash (latency, errors). If any metric crosses threshold -> pause and investigate.
- T+30m: Expand to 5% if green; run sample end-to-end QA journeys.
- T+90m: Expand to 20%. Run a random sample anomaly detection job; check regression evals.
- T+3h: Expand to 50% if stable. Ops rotates next on-call.
- T+6h: Full expansion to 100% if no triggers. Begin quiet-window sampling for 24h.

Monitoring triggers (hard stop conditions) — if any fire, hold expansion and escalate:
- error_rate > 0.5% sustained for > 5m OR 3x baseline
- p95 latency > baseline + 15% for > 10m
- mem pressure > 85% on > 20% of canary hosts
- KV cache hit ratio drops > 20% leading to >2x token cost delta
- any customer-facing incident reported (CS Slack/escalation)

Rollback decision matrix (quick):
- Severity 1 (prod-impacting): immediate rollback to v3.1, page SRE/PL, cut traffic to fallback pool.
- Severity 2 (degradation but not outage): pause expansion, reduce canary to previous stable percentage, triage with serving-runtime.
- Non-critical anomalies: continue, log, schedule hotfix for next patch deploy.

Communication plan (who says what):
- 0-2h: ops lead posts hourly brief in #shipday-ops (status, key metrics).
- 2-6h: SRE posts half-hourly if expansion in progress.
- Any hard stop: @channel + runbook link + incident bridge pinned (ops lead).
- Customer comms: CS on standby; for major regressions, draft template saved as assets/release-comm-template.docx.

Release notes (DRAFT) — marketing-friendly bullets, keep short:
- Feature: model v3.2 rollout — improved coherence for mid-long contexts and 10% lower median latency on generation paths for typical prompt sizes.
- Improvement: default batching policy tuned to reduce small-request tail latency on low-traffic routes.
- Ops: KV cache TTL rationalized to reduce cold-starts for interactive sessions.
- Known issue: under very long single-session prompt streams (>8k tokens) we may see transient memory pressure on small instance types; mitigation: autoscale throttle and fallback to larger instance families.

Annotated issues log (live; fill during watch):
- [ ] ISSUE-1: 07/16 00:12 UTC - canary host restart loop observed on host-id node-a12. Initial: OOM. Notes: process crashed after ~900MB growth in KV snapshot load. Action: bump mem margin on canary pool; add guard to skip heavy-prefetch. Owner: Kenji.
- [ ] ISSUE-2: 07/16 00:40 UTC - p95 latency spike to +22% for route /v1/generate - coincided with cache warming. Notes: evaluate batching throttle; consider temporary rate limit on concurrent requests to that route. Owner: Arjun.
- [ ] ISSUE-3: 07/16 02:10 UTC - alert: error_rate reached 0.6% for 7m. Root cause: third-party tokenization microservice returned 502 for a subset of requests. Mitigation: fail open to internal tokenizer; CS notified. Owner: Sofia.

Post-deploy immediate actions (first 24h):
- [ ] Tag release in GitHub, attach perf artifacts and bench logs. (Arjun)
- [ ] Run nightly regression evals against production traffic sample (bench-team).
- [ ] Schedule retro within 72h with SRE/serving-runtime/infra/customer-success.
- [ ] If any hotfix required, create hotfix branch and aim for <48h turnaround.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we enable prefix-cache prefetch for large customer lists during canary? risk vs reward. (decision needed)
- Add a synthetic customer journey that mirrors high-concurrency, long-prompt sessions to catch mem pressure earlier. (Kenji)
- Validate autoscaler cooldown parameters for dedicated pools under v3.2 - might be too aggressive. (infra)

Back-of-envelope deployment economics note (ops reminder):
- If KV hit drops by 10% at 20% traffic, token-cost delta roughly +7% — scale back canary speed and evaluate quantization profile.

Attachments and references:
- confluence: CONFLUENCE-12345 (detailed rollout plan + historical incident digests)
- jira epic: JIRA-RL-9876 (rollout epic with canary tickets)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123
- smoke scripts: /ops/smoke/smoke-v3.2.sh

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep communications tight and avoid over-expanding traffic if any 2 of the golden metrics drift.
- If third-party tokenizer flaps again, schedule a contingency to run lightweight tokenizer locally during next patch window.
- Remember to capture sampling traces (include model and kernel selection metadata) — those helped last time to root-cause a subtle quantization mismatch.

Next steps before T-30m:
- Ops lead to post final checklist, confirm canary config URL, and verify pager rotations.
- SRE to validate alert thresholds live and run simulated false-positive test.
- Infra to confirm capacity for burstbackfill in us-west and eu-central (reserve 20%).

-- end of briefing --
(keep this file as the working log during the first 12h; I will convert to post-mortem template after stabilizing)
